items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this for a premium documentary YouTube Shorts channel about money, history and the tricks behind them. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller with a hint of mystery: curious, quietly amused, energetic and punchy, never slow, never announcer-like. Natural emphasis on dates and numbers, questions end with a curious lift, a short comic pause before each punchline. Keep the same voice, pace and energy from start to finish. Chars voices two funny cartoon characters (a smug gold bar and a nervous banknote), short and punchy, performed exactly as described in each bracket.
lines: Would you risk prison for a one-million-dollar coin? Three men did, in twenty seventeen. But the million was never the point. Why?
Berlin, three thirty a.m. Thieves climb in from the train tracks and roll Canada's hundred-kilo gold coin out on a wheelbarrow.
So why call it a million-dollar coin?
Because one million is just its face value, in Canadian dollars.
[nervous, squeaky, high-pitched banknote, sudden worried realisation] Wait. Mine's just printed on, too.
The gold inside? Police put it at over four million dollars.
And that's not even the strangest part.
Police believe it was melted and sold. Three men were jailed. The coin was never found.
Since then, gold has more than tripled. Today, those hundred kilos would be worth about thirteen million dollars.
The coin said one million. The gold says thirteen.
[smug, deep, rich gold bar, very pleased with himself] Finally. Someone who knows my worth.
Comment: is your money worth what it says?
This is Money Mirage. Follow for more.
